speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Today, there are many community agencies on the ground providing a variety of support services to those in need, from family matters to financial aid and also healthcare.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As social needs become more complex, individuals in need will require multiple forms of social support, which are being provided by different community agencies today.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This can be an advantage – that agencies specialise in order to help individuals with specific problems.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It increases efficiency and reduces transaction time on the part of people seeking help.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: At the same time, problems do not respect bureaucratic borders – individuals that need help may not necessarily have the time and effort to "code-switch" across these agencies, whether it is about filling up forms or registering for means testing.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Instead, they may delay their applications, sometimes causing their own situation to worsen by the time they seek help.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We do not want our social safety net to fail where it is most crucially needed.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: On the other hand, there are also many different Singaporeans who want to contribute their time and money, but may not be able to commit for the long term, or at regular intervals.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We should not ignore this important group of volunteers which add up to a significant number of volunteer hours.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Again, the complexity exists on the supply end of this issue.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We need some special, specific and granular mechanisms to bridge complexity at both ends – coordination, planning and organisation.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We can all do better if there are plans to help direct these efforts and other community efforts through better coordination and sharing of information about individuals and families in need in the community.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If we fail to coordinate, there will be continued frustration, unmet urgent needs and a general sense of helplessness among many communities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But if we succeed, the outcome is both powerful and simple – a stronger, more beautiful fabric of Singapore, woven by all of us together.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, the Government has put in place many schemes and services to support Singaporeans in building strong families including various marriage preparation programmes for couples looking to get married.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But some young people looking to get married get caught up in the romance and the emotions of the moment.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: They do not have the time nor the inclination to plan and prepare.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Another is titled "PREP" or Prevention and Relationship Enhancement Programme.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am not sure, even after reading the syllabus, exactly what it is that the course is trying to prevent.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But some of the classes, "Negotiation and Conflict Resolution", for example, it is very useful indeed, especially like how the website said that the course was "proven to sustain up to five years" after the programme.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I must assure Members of the House that I support these courses and I do think they are useful.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But we must not approach them in the same benefit-and-cost analysis manner that we do in courses.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If a marriage is abusive and unhappy, surely the best outcome is to step out of it.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Divorce should not be seen as a failure but an option in human relationships.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Strong marriages are important to a nation as well as to couples themselves.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We must start conversations about what strong marriages mean as well as how to build it.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This, to me, is the true benefit of preparation courses.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's social challenges are turning complicated and complex.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The new normal is the recognition that Government can no longer do it alone.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Even the supposedly simple issue of "feeding the hungry" is, in truth, not as simple as it appears.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The recent CNA documentary on "Food Insecurities" showed up problems such as overlapping of help efforts; reluctance of donors to work with each other; and wastage of donated items.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I myself have been involved in issues such as coordinating senior services and helping cardboard collectors in my constituency and district – not easy.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: MSF Minister Desmond Lee himself has personally led in bringing together groups to solve social concerns such as rough sleepers and also food distribution to the poor.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We have to find a formula that goes beyond the interest, passion and intervention of a heroic Minister.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Tackling social challenges together, especially more challenging wicked ones, calls for several critical success factors: a strong sponsor who can back with the right links; a systems thinking approach; clarity in problem statement; an understanding of the overall landscape, driving and restraining forces; a strong facilitator; and implementation discipline for results.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: MSF should be given resources to start an establishment that is nimble and competent enough to facilitate and pull in the right internal and external resources to address identified prioritised social challenges – a SWAT team of sorts.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I seek the Ministry's inputs on how it intends to lead and facilitate the imperative of tackling social challenges together with others in the community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: What are the outcomes and obstacles to date?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, Singapore was ranked by the Economist Intelligence Unit as the fourth most food-secure nation in the world.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: These were the findings of the 2018 report "Hunger in a Food Lover's Paradise" by the Lien Centre for Social Innovation at SMU.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: There were some 125 food support groups operating in Singapore, in addition to food support from ethnic self-help groups and community organisations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: A basic question is how much food is enough.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: More importantly, that study reveals that Singaporeans consider food to be more than calories for the body; it is nourishment for the soul.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It includes having meaningful choice and variety, the opportunity to eat healthily but also enjoy the occasional indulgence and the chance to meet friends at the hawker centre or to invite others to a home-cooked meal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It is not three restaurant meals a day.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Despite good intentions, charity struggles to meet these varied needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Esther, a retiree, told CNA Insider in a report on food insecurity published this month, and I quote: "We can’t give feedback because the food is free… It feels like we are beggars, what they give, we must eat." But Esther has diabetes and high blood pressure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: She needs a healthier diet for her health conditions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: She does not always have a meaningful choice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, with your permission, may I display a slide on the LCD screen.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Ms Diana Ong from the Chinese Development Assistance Council (CDAC) conducted a study under the mentorship of Dr Ong Qiyan from the Social Service Research Centre at NUS.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: The big difference in spending is not in eating out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: It is in trying to eat a healthier home-cooked diet.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: These results are consistent with the food insecurity-obesity paradox: that in a rich country, food insecurity manifests not as starvation, but as an inadequate and unhealthy diet that exposes the poor to risks of obesity and malnutrition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: And when children are affected by a less healthy diet, as in the CDAC study, then these consequences can last a lifetime.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, this cut concerns food insecurity in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Individuals are food insecure when they are not confident of having economic and physical access to sufficient acceptable food for a healthy life.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: CNA recently did a feature on food insecure families as cited by Members previously, and I have three specific questions.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Thirdly, what efforts are being taken by the Ministry to ensure that our food insecure households are able to afford healthy and nutritious food?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: What additional investment is required to improve access to nutritious food?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Does the Ministry intend to make these investments?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Households living in landed property, who spent nearly 5% more on average every year between 2008 and 2013, tightened the purse strings to spending just 0.2% more every year between 2013 and 2018.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If this trend continues, it does not bode well for the financial well-being of lower income households even when income inequality is mitigated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Tracking such data can help MSF provide better and targeted assistance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is much higher than the 8.1% on average for all HDB households.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is quite anomalous and warrants study, as housing costs should be a progressive burden and not tax the lower income more.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, the past two years have seen the production of several media shows that highlighted the complex social issues that Singapore faces, and in that process, offered us a deeper glimpse into the challenges and struggles that some Singapore families have to grapple with.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Channel News Asia’s thought-provoking documentaries, "Don’t Call Us Poor", "Inside the Children’s ICU", and "Inside the Child Protective Service" have highlighted the crucial point that there will never be a simple solution, there will never be a simple solution to tackle social issues because of the inherent complex inter-dependencies that reside in them.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Indeed, these could be what philosopher and management scholar, C West Churchman, referred to as "wicked problems".

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Classic examples of wicked problems include economic, environmental, political and social problems whose solution requires a great number of actors to come together to deliver a holistic whole-of-the-problem solution.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Wicked problems are impossible to resolve in a piecemeal manner as the inherent complex inter-dependencies that exist between the variables in these problems will render any effort to solve one aspect of the problem to reveal or create other problems.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Singapore has always adopted the "many helping hands" approach when it comes to community assistance.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many community agencies on the ground provide a variety of support services to those in need, from family matters to financial aid and even healthcare.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As social needs become more complex however, individuals and families in need may require multiple forms of social support, which could be provided by different community agencies today.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: There are many families who are in need in our society.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: They face many issues, such as financial inadequacy, poor health, low education, unemployment, single parenthood, many members to support, physical or mental disability and so on.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many families, when faced with multiple problems and stresses, become overwhelmed and ill equipped to care and provide for their children.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: These children will not enjoy the same fighting chance as their better-off peers, and thus may grow up to be in the same predicament as their parents if intervention and help are not rendered in time or in a sustainable manner.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: These families require intensive, holistic and coordinated assistance.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Would MSF look into the following issues of such families?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Has there been any survey done to see how many of such families who are in need?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: We need to know who they are before we can reach out to them.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Can MSF provide the resources for good outreach to touch base with these families, to understand their needs, to assist them with their urgent needs and to coordinate and follow-up with them in a sustainable manner?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: These families need intense hand holding, because just informing them on the many assistance schemes that they can tap on will not work for them.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Two, do we have plans and effective programmes in place that are able to collectively solve the needs of these families in areas such as financial, education of children, medical health referrals, childcare placement, re-employment and so on.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: More social workers who can understand the needs of each family, sorting out the families' issues; by tapping into the various Government schemes, by working and coordinating with social service agencies (SSAs) to benefit these families.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Three, do we have an upstream measure in place to handhold such families?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of these families have disadvantaged children that need longer follow-up, especially the young children.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The reason is that such families may have entrenched problems that cannot be solved overnight.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Priority must be given to their children in their well-being as they grow up especially in their education, health and character development.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Our system must be robust to ensure that these children are on track to get out of their families' predicament and the chance to climb the social ladder or to break the poverty cycles.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Evidence shows that the developmental years, especially the first few years of a child's life are fundamentally important.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Special attention and assistance given to the first few years of children's lives lead to better economic, social and emotional benefits later on.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: In disadvantaged families, many parents are unable to support their children's education due to limited resources and their own educational level.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Others tend to be permissive and take a hands-off approach.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: These families and children need closer follow-up and supervision by MSF.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Five, many community agencies on the ground can be roped in to provide a variety of support services to those families in need, from family matters to financial aid and even healthcare.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: As social needs become more complex, individuals in needs may require multiple forms of social support, which could be provided by the different community agencies today.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Are there plans to help direct these efforts through better coordination and sharing of information about individuals or families in need in the community?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Comprehensive assistance can be facilitated by data and digital technologies, on implementations and on follow-up.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I hope MSF can facilitate the adoption and wider use of such technology.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: This will enable good coordination and good outreach to families in need by the various agencies, but more importantly, it is to spread the resources for better coverage and to prevent duplication or uneven distribution of help.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Social service agencies are critical partners in providing such support programmes and services to help individuals and families overcome their difficult circumstances.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The social service sector will have to adopt more productive and innovative processes, as well as continually build up new competencies.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: What are the Ministry's plans to strengthen capability development amongst social service agencies, to meet growing social needs?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Can there be priority given to these families to assist their children better?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Apart from assisting their children's education and well-being, the spouses of these families also require hand holding assistance in finding employment.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I quote the hon Member of Parliament, Dr Lily Neo on a speech during the COS debates in 2018.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She said, "Many of them may have a variety of problems, such as family feuds, HDB housing issues, mental issues, employment and financial issues".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In response, the hon Minister for Social and Family Development, Mr Desmond Lee stated, "We need a more coordinated, whole-of-society approach to address the underlying issues and needs of these individuals.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: MSF works closely with other frontline agencies and the community to reach out and coordinate the help that they need." This approach makes eminent sense.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The report also identified that a good number of rough sleepers have residences but decided not to stay at home for one reason or another.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I tried to persuade the rough sleeper, who refused to go back home owing to a combination of family and mental health issues, to go to a shelter instead.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Over time, he became more and more frail.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Now he is missing and that is doubly concerning.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: With the rough sleeper brought into institutionalised care, I would think there will consequently be a better opportunity to resolve the underlying issues that gave rise to him not returning to his residence.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I wish to stress though that any exercise of power under the Act must be done with the health and welfare of the rough sleeper in mind.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Chairman, the "Break the Silence" campaign which you launched when you were Minister has brought crucial awareness to domestic violence issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: While many domestic violence cases fall within traditional family contexts, vulnerable groups, such as LGBTQ+ persons, face specific challenges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: The NGO Sayoni found that LBTQ women are at increased risk of facing domestic violence, but they do not often seek help, due to the fear of disclosing their stigmatised identity and a lack of understanding that state institutions will protect them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Initiatives like "Break the Silence" often do not explicitly include LGBTQ+ persons in the campaign resources.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: If vulnerable groups are not represented or acknowledged, they are less likely to seek help as they may not believe their specific needs will be addressed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: In 2016, The Straits Times reported that social workers "feel ill-equipped to deal with LGBT clients".

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Sayoni's research found LBTQ persons face additional challenges in seeking help because social workers may lack a sensitive understanding of their identities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: For instance, Jamie, who was experiencing psychological violence from her family, approached an area-based counselling service for anger management issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: The counsellor did not directly address Jamie's anger management problem, but instead, offered to address the, I quote, "gay problem", thereby framing being gay as the cause of Jamie's distress.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: The possibility of being misunderstood or discriminated against by social workers deters many LGBTQ+ persons from seeking help.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Could the Ministry provide in-depth sensitivity training for social workers and other first responders to address the specific needs of these marginalised groups?

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Hon Members, it is my right today to speak to you for four minutes and no longer.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Just as it is our right as Singaporeans to contest elections to enter this House or in my case, to be appointed.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Fundamentally, rights are legal, social, or ethical principles of freedom or entitlement, stipulating what is allowed of people or owed to people according to legal doctrine, social convention or ethical theory.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Identity protection for all our children is critical in a digitalising age.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: For today's young people, the digital world is ripe with opportunity but fraught with risk.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I would thus like to highlight the issue of the digital rights of children.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: When I started researching into young people's media use 20 years ago, I was speaking to teens.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: In my most recent research, some of my interviewees reached just above my knee.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Indeed, with device use creeping ever lower, we must think of more concerted protection for our children from commercial and sexual exploitation on online platforms.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Children are the target of media content that shows the unboxing of attractive toys they cannot afford and the allure of fast food, fast fashion and unhealthy habits such as vaping.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Young people's data is being collected and used for commercial purposes and they are aggresively marketed to across all platforms, including movies, internet connected toys, apps, online games and social media.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Even in the face of COVID-19, I believe our children are under greater threat of from influencers than from influenza!

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: More egregiously, young people are also the target of sexual grooming in online platforms and exposure to sexually explicit content.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: In Singapore, we have done well to ensure children's rights to access digital devices, services and digital literacy education to children from all socio-economic backgrounds.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: One key issue is that the terms and conditions of digital products and services are couched in obtuse language that adults cannot understand, let alone children.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Importantly, we should also involve our young people in the process of identifying what they believe their digital rights currently are and should be.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: For differently-abled children in particular, we must also develop more schemes to pioneer innovation so that they too can enjoy greater access to digital devices and services.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our children are the future capital of our nation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is therefore important that we provide them with the resources to achieve their maximum potential in life, regardless of the starting point that they are born into.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, not every child is fortunate enough to be born into an environment filled with love.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To help this group of vulnerable children, Parliament amended the Children and Young Persons Act in 2019, to strengthen support for children who have been neglected or abused.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Various studies on at-risk youths in Singapore has found that peer and family influence may have an impact in influencing youths' attitudes towards gangs and juvenile delinquency.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We should therefore work towards identifying early signposts that would identify a child to be at-risk, and adopt a more preventive and integrative approach towards helping them and their families.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Beyond the Government’s effort, I also urge community groups to come together to rally our youths and help them stay out of trouble.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One good example of a community initiative targeting at-risk youths is the Delta League programme.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Created in 2011, Delta League engages our youths through football during the long June and December school holidays.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To keep them meaningfully occupied and away from crime, besides attending football clinics and playing matches, the youths also participate in crime prevention and other activities to enhance their awareness of crime and its consequences.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some of our Delta League boys have since gone on to fulfill their dreams of becoming professional footballers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With support from MSF, I hope to see more of such initiatives from the ground to help our at-risk youths in this new decade.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, we can and we must, help our vulnerable groups of children and at-risk youths to achieve their maximum potential in life, regardless of their starting point.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Government has also issued Enabling Masterplans and the leadership of some colleagues in this House towards realising this vision is well-known.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Recently a disabled resident asked me to raise the topic of training and employment prospects for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Non-governmental organisations also have initiatives such as sheltered workshops to provide training and employment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: He will be three years old in April.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Time really flies but I remember vividly the emotions I felt when my husband and I were figuring out how to support his developments.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We have a challenging start but found most of the information, guidance and support we needed online, through talking other parents and people in the sector.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: SG Enable was one of the agencies which my husband and I became familiar with very earlier on in our journey.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We were informed about SG Enable through the social worker at the hospital and she helped us apply for the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC) through SG Enable.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In the course of my work as Member of Parliament, I found out more about the work that is done by SG Enable, especially in providing information and referral services of various schemes and providing employment support for persons with disabilities (PWDs).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe that over the years, SG Enable has started to establish itself as a trusted partner to PWDs, their care-givers and social service agencies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is important to build on this and make the infrastructure and services more pervasive and accessible to families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Parents sometimes find that the services and spaces that are conducive for their children with needs are not located to where they live.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It would be ideal if more spaces like Enabling Village, for example, could be replicated all around Singapore.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: SPD President Ms Chia Yong Yong, a PWD herself and me in my volunteering capacity as ARC President and a parent of a PWD co-chair the workgroup with Minister of State Mr Sam Tan.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I would also like to focus on three other issues which are not covered by the two workgroups.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: First on life of PWDs after their parents' death.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: One common grievance by families with children with disabilities is the question of, “What would happen to my child when I am no longer around?” I have heard this at many focus groups for the last 20 years.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Their worries range from financial, legal, housing, healthcare and other issues.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: In recent years, there are books, portals and even agencies to help families plan for the future.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: However, if these families are still living with worry and fear, then there is more to be done in this space.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Next, on residential options of adults with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The current options of where adult PWDs can live and be supported appropriately, are too limiting.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: PWDs are expected to live with their families, with whoever relatives are left or in costly residential homes for those with higher support needs and less family support.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The existing models do not cater sufficiently to a continuum of adult PWDs with varying support needs and abilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Some interesting models like the TOUCH Ubi Hostel for PWDs are some of the best kept secrets in the community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Singapore is unique in itself in the social eco-system.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Public housing is the pride of the nation and every Singaporean is encouraged to own a home.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: This will empower PWDs and families to make their choices and become part of the solution.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Research has shown that although most people in Singapore welcome the idea of an inclusive society, not everyone is willing to or feel comfortable interacting with PWDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Both the disability community and the rest of Singapore need to organise ourselves better for better outcomes in community access and inclusion.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Can Government streamline Government-linked agencies so that there is less overlap and greater clarity to the public on the "who", the "what" and the "how" in disability support and inclusion?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Can more "mainstream" services be tapped upon to increase the presence and inclusion of PWDs?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: For instance, can the community clubs and the grassroots movement identify PWDs and include they and their families in their midst of their activities and their plans?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Can a continuum of housing options for PWDs be designed into all new and existing public housing estates so that PWDs can live with the appropriate support there, seeing and be heard and felt?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Can every Government ministry appoint Disability Champions or teams to look out for and include PWDs in both their work and other parts of life?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is a basic societal tenet that we should provide all children with opportunities to learn, grow and contribute to society.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We need to further enhance support for children with special needs and disabilities, especially those who have early childhood intervention is especially critical.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Moreover, EIPIC programmes are usually not integrated with mainstream childcare programmes, where educators are largely not trained to teach children with special needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: As a result, the children may feel excluded and be deterred from interacting or participating.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Such disjointed arrangements also exact a toll on working parents who have to shuttle their children back and forth from EIPIC centres to childcare and it also wears the children out as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I will like to suggest a couple of approaches to improve the system capacity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: One, we need to have more inclusive pre-schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The initial slower pace is only to be expected because we need mainstream acceptance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Alternatively, we can consider widening the eligibility for pre-school/childcare subsidies to more private operators of schools for students with special needs under the Enhanced Pilot for Private Intervention Providers scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Two, we can leverage on the childcare anchor operators by providing subsidies to train their educators, hire specialist therapists and upgrade their facilities to be inclusive schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Three, we can also consider having special needs care as one of the components of teachers’ basic training.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs) offer subsidised before and after school care services for students with special needs aged seven years to 18 years.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: They are key to providing care-giving and educational support and skills for independent living for these Special Education (SPED) students.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: With the support of SSCCs, parents have more options and time available to them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: SPED students are also given more opportunities to interact with their community and plan for their future.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: However, the number of such SSCCs remains small.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We need to ensure that such services remain affordable.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Although subsidies are available for those who need them, the fees quickly run into the hundreds of dollars, with surcharges during school holiday periods.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Families with special needs children already face many challenges.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Surely, we can support them better, especially when the systems are already in place.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: So, I like to ask the Minister what measures are in place to ensure that SSCCs remain affordable for families who require these services, especially for those with multiple needs?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I would like to address the challenges of teenage health, both physical and emotional, and the necessary roles that parents can play in providing a nurturing and loving environment to secure a bright future for their offsprings.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Teens in Singapore face a multitude of issues ranging from body image, struggles to find their place in society, peer influence, parental pressure, physical health changes, school-related stress, bullying, substance abuse, just to name a few.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Healthcare professionals caring for school-aged children and adolescents are also seeing an increased cases of eating disorders, a form of psychiatric illness with significant, life-threatening medical complications as well as teenage suicide cases.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Although there are many contributing factors to these problems, I believe that parents can do more to help and support their teenagers in this challenging journey.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, there is a need for us to work on and improve parenting skills of our adults in Singapore because I believe that all parents want the best for their children.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure that all parents in this Chamber, myself included, will agree that parenting is one of the most complex jobs out there.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: There is a widely held and unfounded perception that parents should or naturally know what to do to parent their children and everything will be fine as long as we love them enough.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: But I am sorry to say that this is not always the case.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: As such, I find it quite perplexing that we are not using available science, expertise and valuable experiences from those who have gone through the journey to better prepare new parents.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Parenting courses will be useful to help new parents eliminate unnecessary fears of unknowns while bringing awareness to what may be expected when raising a child.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: It will also help them understand and learn different parenting styles for different personalities and how to engage their kids to create a supportive family structure through mindfulness and conscious parenting.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: At the end of the day, we should prepare our kids for what lies ahead by providing them with a strong mental, emotional and moral foundation.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: We cannot just leave this to MOE or MSF alone because no one can be a better role model to our children than us, parents.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: As a working mother with four children, I can fully understand that this is not easy.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: We cannot be perfect but we must keep trying and keep working on it, using the right parenting skills – like speaking to my kids sitting in the Gallery today.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: I have attended such courses at my children's schools and a common remark from the teachers at the start of the course is that, often, the parents who do not make time or do not have the time for these programmes are the ones that the teachers need to reach out to.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: This brings me to an enlightened quote from Dr Shefali Tsabary, a renowned clinical psychologist and writer of the award-winning New York Times bestselling book, "The Conscious Parent – Transforming Ourselves, Empowering our Children".

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: Her revolutionary wisdom focuses on a parent-centric way of upbringing, rather than on the child.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: And I end with a quote, "To be an awakened parent who is aware that traditional paradigms of parenting, where parent is seen as greater than the child are obsolete in the modern world, producing dysfunction and disconnections in families.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: When parents are aware in the present moment, learning and growing alongside their children, the entire family thrives.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: Free to actualise their individual destiny, each family member lives unencumbered and unafraid.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: Empowered with self-awareness, boundless in self-belief, liberated in self-expression, each feels free to explore, discover and manifest their authentic being."

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We often hear of how children become embroiled in your parents' acrimonious divorce proceedings and are made emotional pawns.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I am a lawyer in family practice and I see that happening often.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In such situations, I often ask my client to think about the child's best interests.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Divorcing parties are, however, often caught up in their emotions and are not able to think rationally.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: One area that is particularly challenging relates to arrangements of custody, care and control and access of the children.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It would help processes in the family justice system better support divorcing parties and encourage more positive outcomes and arrangements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That is ideal but the reality is that a divorcing couple might find it hard to cooperate on an issue as contentious as housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Divorce rulings already decide on custody, care and control and division of matrimonial assets, which are equally contentious.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can MSF clarify what each parent awarded care and control is expected to provide in terms of housing for the child?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is a parent's ability to provide housing a factor in awarding care and control to that parent?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, the parent who needs the cash component of the Baby Bonus the most is the one who does not qualify for it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They can get the cash if they marry the father or mother of their child and then file for a divorce.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But why do we want fellow citizens to marry someone they do not want to marry and jump through so many hoops to get something they should get?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They already receive the CDA component of the Baby Bonus, so why not the cash component?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Over the years, the Government has been providing generous pre-school subsidies to support working parents with young children in their care-giving duties.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This has allowed many women to re-join the workforce after becoming mothers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: So, helping these women return to work is a significant and worthwhile effort.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Many women already know of the platforms that are in place to help them, including subsidies from MOM as well as social enterprises who link them up with employment opportunities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: These women may already have strong social networks.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: However, there is a gap for low-income mothers who do not have alternative care-giving arrangements.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: For those who do not work, they may not know of these platforms and opportunities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: And this may, in turn, affect their ability to look for paid employment opportunities that are flexible enough to accommodate their need to care for their young children.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This sets up a vicious cycle of missed opportunities and lack of mobility.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Do we know how large this group is and what are the main obstacles to their re-joining the workforce?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This is the group that needs more help from us.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister what other measures are in place to better support this group of low-income mothers who do not have alternative care-giving arrangements.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to speak in Mandarin for my first cut.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   	Because of COVID-19, some of our expatriate pre-school Chinese teachers must be quarantined and cannot return to Singapore to resume work.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Their colleagues who continue working and their students all miss them.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They are being told not to worry as the pre-school centres are working hard to ensure that students can attend lessons as usual.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During this critical period, everyone is working together to overcome difficulties.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I understand recruiting Singaporean pre-school Chinese teachers is a challenge.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have met many Singaporeans who are passionate about the Chinese language and some of them are mid-career individuals.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must also provide schemes for upskilling, as well as education resources, to help Chinese language teachers gain new knowledge and deepen their teaching capabilities to help nurture students' interest in the Chinese language.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In 2018, MSF announced a new Mother Tongue teaching certification programme jointly launched by ECDA and the National Institute of Early Childhood Development.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The programme was launched last year with the aim of enhancing the oral skills of pre-school teachers and deepening their understanding of the relevant cultures and traditions.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The programme will cater to Malay and Tamil teachers initially.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Does the Ministry also track the pricing of fees by all registered centres and publish this information for comparison by parents?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In a recent response from MSF to my Parliamentary Question, it was noted that close to half of parents' feedback concerning SCCs are related to issues, such as hygiene and child management.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The rest relates to affordability, capacity and issues, such as enrolment process, to the requirements imposed on registered SCCs.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently MSF only provides SCC operators guidelines in aspects, such as staffing, layout, programme, hygiene and safety, recommended educational qualifications and training for their supervisors and staff.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: All SCCs are also required to meet standards in the areas of supervision, physical environment, operating hours, safety, health and hygiene and provide a structured daily programme.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Ministry consider mirroring the approach taken in the pre-school sector?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Childcare centres and kindergartens are licensed under the regulatory framework.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This helps to enhance the affordability, accessibility and quality of our pre-schools.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Consequently, there are also clear skills frameworks and mandatory training programmes to ensure that there is uniformity in how pre-school centres deliver their care and supervision programmes.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe this can serve as a useful guide to the SCCs to provide a positive and developmentally appropriate physical environment for our students.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With a better trained workforce and clearer career progression, it can also seek to improve the professional image of the student care sector and attract more Singaporeans to join the sector.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Ministry consider having funding support to assist the centres invest in staff training so that we can have a sound and reliable after-school care support system?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Darryl David, take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, a research on neurology and developmental psychology found that the early years of a child's learning experience plays an important role in the child's future physical, cognitive, emotional and social development.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Early childhood education, therefore, has a direct impact on the child's overall development, the type of adult that he/she will become and the society that a country will develop accordingly.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In his research, Jack Shonkoff of the Harvard School of Public Health went as far as to suggest that early childhood education is the most important investment that a country can make because it forms the foundations for a prosperous and sustainable society.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is because a stable, responsive, rich and nurturing learning experience in the formative years of a child will have a lifelong impact on his/her mental and physical health, as well as the human capital potential.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Beyond the Government's plans to expand the Anchor Operators (AOPs) and POPs in the early childhood sector, how else is the Government intending to support other pre-school operators, especially the smaller independent ones in this sector?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Government has made significant investments in recent years to enhance the quality and accessibility of early childhood education.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In last year's National Day Rally, as I have mentioned earlier, Prime Minister highlighted the broad plans to "more than double" the current spending on early childhood education over the next few years.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Under the current framework, a larger subsidy quantum is given to working mothers to support their child care-giving needs when they are at work.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In contrast, a smaller subsidy quantum is given to non-working mothers with the understanding that they provide home-based care-giving to their children as an alternative to full-day childcare services.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This has resulted in a somewhat unique situation sometimes where dual-income families could receive a higher level of pre-school subsidies than single-income families.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to state for the record that I am very grateful for all the hard work that my wife does as a full-time mum, a non-working mum, and I agree that non-working mothers could provide the home-based childcare giving that working mothers are unable to.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, the reality is that not all working mothers are able to provide effective home-based care for various reasons such as having to meet the demands of caring for elderly family members, who are old or who have special-needs; or in fact, caring for their other children whom might have special needs as well.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As much as we would like to believe that every child has the potential to succeed and do well in life, in reality, the circumstances in which the child is in at the start of his or her life, could dictate this trajectory of the life journey.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: His or her future could be impacted even as early as when the child is in the mother's womb.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The mother's nutrition during her pregnancy will have an effect on a child's health and development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The child's well-being and development will be affected by stimulations the child receives.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have now identified the importance of early childhood education and how crucial the early years are in shaping his or her development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I have always been excited about KidSTART and the potential it brings to change the lives of many children from low-income families and those who have challenging backgrounds.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This programme provides holistic and comprehensive support to these families and gives these children a fighting chance to seize the same opportunities as children from better-off families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Further, in this regard, could MSF provide any updates on the types of partnerships with corporate and community partners forged thus far and whether we could build on these partnerships?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Mr Chairman, at one of our Clementi coffeeshops, on weekends you can find a very special group of uncles and aunties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Some come from all over Singapore to meet.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Some from the Pioneer Generation, some from the Merdeka Generation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Each one a veteran artist with a lifetime of experience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: A number have even won the Cultural Medallion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: All these luminaries and legends – and you can find them at one of our Clementi coffeeshops on a weekend.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Last year, as part of our National Day celebrations, these veteran artists helped organise an exhibition at our Clementi Community Centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: It was a very special gathering, but what made it extra special, even more special, was how our residents came together, across from all walks of life, with the artists for this community art exhibition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Exhibiting artworks together, even making impromptu artwork on the spot together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Young parents, youths, children from all walks of life, including families, starting with less, families living in our rental blocks in Clementi.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: I spoke with a young boy, who was deeply moved that his drawing was being exhibited alongside the work of these famous artists.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: The artists also shared, that by connecting with the community, including some of our children who were starting with less, they had also found ways to introduce their heritage, their life stories to another generation of young Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: When people come together, creating moments, creating memories, creating opportunity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We see this too, in our tuition mentoring programmes in Clementi Town.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Young professionals, as well as students still in higher education, young people working together, volunteering as homework mentors for children who are starting with less.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: And with each friendship forged, each moment shared, it lifts up each child even as it changes, touches, transforms the life of each volunteer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: It tells us that how we multiply social capital is an important complement to the traditional fiscal measures that can found in any Budget.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Because, Mr Chairman, in a fair and equitable society, fiscal redistribution is an important part of policy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Fiscal redistribution in a progressive way, giving more to people who start with less.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: But there are also many kinds of sharing, many kinds of sharing which go beyond dollars and cents which cannot easily be measured in terms of hard numbers, but these forms of sharing are also deeply important.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: The sharing of life experiences, the sharing of networks, the sharing of mentorship, the sharing of social capital.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: And Sir, it is my belief that this element of social capital can and must be part of how we continue building and uplifting our communities and our societies because, whether in Singapore or around the world, much of the research on the role of neighbourhoods, on the role of communities, implicit in that, is the idea that in that in the role of places and neighbourhoods, there is also the role of social capital.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Because, Mr Chairman, as we said earlier when we share social capital it multiplies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: So, let us grow our society and multiply the good within us to touch others.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their thoughtful and heartfelt speeches.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the last few years, we have been working with many community partners and stakeholders to transform our social sector, better enable Singaporeans to seize opportunities and uplift those who have encountered setbacks, at every stage of their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF will continue to push ahead with efforts to transform our social safety net in three significant ways.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we will go upstream and intervene early, where possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Intensive downstream measures or casework remains necessary to support those who have fallen behind.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But I think we all agree that prevention is better than cure.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we will continue to put individuals and families at the centre of our work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Not agencies and organisations but people and families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The needs of families and individuals can be complex and inter-locking.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They can seldom be addressed by a single organisation on its own.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Yet, as we bring in more partners, we also need to make sure that it is simple and intuitive for families to access help and resources.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we will continue to streamline structures and processes, tighten coordination across partners and organise services around families and individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, we will reach out and work with even more partners to transform our social safety net together and to address the challenges in the social sector that Deputy Prime Minister mentioned in his Budget Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In order to achieve greater impact, we have to reach out, build relationships, earn the trust of our partners, collaborate and draw on the diverse strengths of the people, private and public partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To facilitate such partnerships, we will build capability, tap on technology to strengthen links between partners and grow organic local community networks.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, let me share some details about how we are pushing ahead in some of these areas.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, expanding our early intervention efforts, to give every child and every family a good start.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The early years are critical for a child's development.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the past decade, we have made significant progress in making quality preschools more accessible and affordable for Singaporean families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also support our Anchor and Partner operators to keep their fees below the caps set by ECDA and invest in improving the quality of their programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the new term, we intend to appoint more.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When we do so, we will further lower the fee caps, so families with children attending these centres can pay lower fees for quality preschool education.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For low-income families, we provide upstream support to them and their children through KidSTART.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since 2016, KidSTART has benefited over 1,000 children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In conjunction with this, we launched the "GROWING TOGETHER with KidSTART" movement where individuals and organisations can contribute directly to the growth and development of children from lower income households.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If you join us, you can partner families, the community and the Government to provide extra resources and support and watch these children grow up.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope more of you will step forward and work with us to give our children the best possible start in life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is again one of the social sector challenges that Deputy Prime Minister referred to in his Budget Statement – to grow a whole-of-society effort to better support children from lower income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our efforts to give every child a good foundation go beyond pre-school.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Working parents may not have time to supervise their children after school.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, will share more details later.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last September, Parliament amended the Children and Young Persons Act.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The raising of the age limit for children and young persons from 16 to 18 years will enable more children to benefit from care, protection and rehabilitation, if needed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim will elaborate on this in his speech.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will now touch on what we are doing to go upstream, to strengthen and support families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: A strong marriage is the foundation for a strong family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Marriage preparation programmes help couples build a strong foundation for their married life and pick up useful skills such as communication and conflict management.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked how we are making these programmes more accessible and affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To encourage more couples to take up such programmes, we have been providing generous rebates and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When couples start a family and become parents, they will face a new set of challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Evidence-based parenting programmes, such as the Positive Parenting Programme or Triple P, have helped parents to pick up skills to manage difficult behaviours exhibited by their children and to reduce their parenting stress.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Irene Quay asked for an update on Triple P, in front of her children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: After we saw how it helped parents, we expanded it to more schools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: An online option for Triple P, or Triple P Online, is also available for the convenience of parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides working with schools in their regions to deliver Triple P to more parents, these providers also serve as a one-stop shop offering a wider range of programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This allows PSPs to provide more customised support for each family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These moves incorporate feedback that we have received – that early support is important to help parents pick up skills for more effective parenting.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As families get smaller, and increasingly both parents work, it can be challenging for families to strike a balance between work and family life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we will do more to give families early support in their parenting journey.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked about the status of the recommendations made by the Committee to Review and Enhance Reforms in the Family Justice System.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have accepted the Committee's recommendations, which include more upstream pre-divorce support for couples.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The feedback and our assessment have been uploaded on the Internet.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the course of marriage, there will be couples who face significantly more challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will develop an online portal to support these couples.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The portal will make it easier to access marriage counselling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope that this will help couples to make better decisions and to give their marriage another chance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But for those who decide to proceed with the divorce, the portal will consolidate information and resources on housing, finance and other important issues that will significantly impact the family's lives after divorce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This helps couples to better understand the practical implications of their decision and reduces the need for couples to approach multiple agencies for information.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Children are often the most severely affected in a divorce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The portal will help couples understand the immediate as well as long-term impact on children, learn how to co-parent effectively and point them to relevant services, if needed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, divorcing parents with minor children, who are unable to reach an agreement on divorce are required to attend the Mandatory Parenting Programme (MPP) where counsellors from the Divorce Support Specialist Agencies (DSSAs) help them better understand the practical issues of divorce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will ride on the online portal to introduce an enhanced Mandatory Parenting Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will help divorcing parties better understand their specific circumstances and needs through an e-learning module, and have a more personalised discussion with their counsellor.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, some couples are hesitant to use face-to-face counselling services or prefer online avenues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This pilot can reach out to 200 clients a year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope that this online channel will encourage those who are hesitant about face-to-face services to seek help earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will assess the demand and the response to this service, before making it available on the online portal itself.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To ensure that the online portal is truly useful, relevant and sensitive, we will engage Singaporeans in focus group discussions in the third quarter of this year to seek honest feedback and develop various aspects of the portal such as design, content and flow.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether MSF could require divorce rulings to specify which parent can list their child as an essential occupier when applying to buy an HDB BTO flat.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I think the Member asked the same question yesterday during MND's COS and also got his answer.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It involves their children and they will be co-parents for the lives of their children as they grow up.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is where the initiatives I just described – the portal, online counselling – could help them work out the best care arrangements for their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Having said that, the Member is right that not all divorces are amicable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB is prepared to consider waiving the mutual agreement requirement if there is clear evidence that one party has already moved on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And the Courts ultimately have the power to make care and control orders and impose conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Parties may return to Court for detailed rulings, if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked about single unwed parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We recognise the challenges faced by single parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is why benefits to support the growth and development of children are given to parents of all Singaporean children, regardless of their marital status.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides the Child Development Account benefits, we have also extended 16 weeks of maternity leave to unwed mothers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last year, we announced that we would be integrating the oversight of early intervention services for children with special needs, with mainstream pre-school services, under one body – the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ECDA will have a holistic view of the developmental needs of children below the age of seven.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They will be able to coordinate early childhood development and early intervention as one integrated continuum.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a next step, we will further streamline the administration of disability functions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through our conversations with the community, we recognise that it can be challenging for persons with disabilities (PWDs) and their care-givers to approach different agencies for different needs and different issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will strengthen the delivery of services for PWDs and their care-givers across different life stages and needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF's Disability Office will retain policy oversight over disability matters.
