speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to work closely with our stakeholders to see how we can better meet the needs of persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last year, we formed three Enabling Masterplan workgroups to look at Employment and Employability, Independent Living and Inclusive Pre-schools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Minister of State Sam Tan will provide updates on these three cross-sectoral workgroups in his speech later.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In our community engagements, we often hear the worries and concerns of care-givers of persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For students with special needs, care-givers tell us that special student care service is essential.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides helping care-givers to balance work and care-giving responsibilities, the service also helps to reinforce what is taught in school.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Minister of State Sam Tan will provide you the details later.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked whether we track the financial health of families at the bottom income quintile as their expenses seem to be growing faster than their incomes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Lower income families also seem to be spending more on household and utilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, some of these families are retiree households who tap on other sources of income, including savings, allowances from children, CPF payouts and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, in calculating household expenditure and utilities, rent is included, but mortgage repayment for owner-occupied property is not.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many 1- to 2-room HDB flats are public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is why families living in these flats seem to be spending more on housing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In any event, for low-income families experiencing hardship, we provide financial assistance, along with the support from our community partners and agencies, to help them with daily expenses and household bills, including utilities, public rental fees and mobile data plans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We regularly review the assistance to account for changes in the prices of essential items as well as changing needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira and Mr Mohamed Irshad asked how we will assist families who face food insecurity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our assistance to low-income families through ComCare covers basic needs such as food.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For families facing immediate needs, our Social Service Offices (SSOs) offer interim assistance such as cash and supermarket vouchers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also connect them to community-based support such as free cooked food.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Families who are unable to buy or prepare their own meals are also linked up with food rations and meal delivery services offered by social service agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We recognise that low-income households may face challenges in eating healthily.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) works with donors to encourage them to donate healthier and more nutritious food products.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The community, too, plays an important role in supporting vulnerable households with food provisions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF has been working with food support organisations and charities since 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last year, we convened a workgroup with food organisations and charities, volunteer groups and Government agencies to look at how to reduce food waste and inefficiencies in distributing food, in order to ensure that beneficiaries receive healthy and nutritious food.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have made some progress and will continue to work on these issues together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we want to go beyond providing financial assistance and addressing immediate needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For families with young children, we want to proactively reach out to provide Comprehensive, Convenient and Coordinated support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We want to empower them to overcome their challenges, achieve sustained stability and possibly even purchase their own homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we want to bring the community together to do this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In each location, we wanted to bring partners together to address the community's needs in a proactive and customised manner.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Darryl David and Dr Lily Neo asked how we work with different community agencies to support individuals and families in need in a more coordinated manner.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our approach is to work with these agencies as equal partners right from the get go.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Backend, the workgroups held regular case discussions to link families to the right agencies for additional support, coordinate the interventions provided and track their progress closely.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For areas that existing programmes may not fully address, the workgroups roped in new partners to bring new programmes to the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we noticed that families in Boon Lay lacked conducive study spaces at home.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Often, parents are also not able to guide their children academically.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In Jalan Kukoh and Marsiling, we have dedicated ComLink centres to run these programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also make full use of existing community resources.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, in Boon Lay and Kembangan-Chai Chee, where the centres are being set up, we maximise existing spaces like the Residents' Network and RCs to operate these community programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Not only Government and community partners are involved.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Corporates and volunteers have stepped forward to offer their expertise and time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Doctors and lawyers have stepped forward to provide free health screening and legal advice to residents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Students from Polytechnics and Universities run tuition and enrichment programmes for the children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ComLink is a good example of the type of cross-sectoral partnerships that can bear fruit when we come together to address specific needs in our local communities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ComLink is a microcosm of how our future social safety net will look like – proactive, upstream, integrated and with individuals and the families placed at the centre of what we do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MTI's assessment, as you heard during their COS, is that the economic impact of COVID-19 could be worse than SARS.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Government has introduced measures to help businesses with cash flow, help workers remain employed and provide additional support for specific sectors directly affected.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For MSF, our priority is to support vulnerable families and individuals who are unable to meet their basic needs because they are unable to work or because the sector they are working in have taken a big hit.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For social service agencies, ComChest will also be providing support to help them cope with additional expenses.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond the challenges it poses to our economy, COVID-19 is also a test of our social resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I am encouraged to see people stepping forward to help one another.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many have signed up to volunteer and donated generously to The Courage Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last Sunday, volunteers in the Families for Life Council launched the "Share-the-Care" movement, which encourages families to look beyond themselves to show appreciation to our frontline and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In fact, I got a message from one of the families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Their son, who is in Secondary school, after playing the games with his parents, packed the basket with new things, went to one of the clinics, after it closed to give it to the doctor and said, "This is for you and your family and children".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, let us continue to stay vigilant, take the necessary precautions, take care of our families and keep a look out for one another and give each other a pat on the back, especially our frontline workers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Denise Phua asked how we are tackling social challenges together as a society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The third key thrust of our transformation is indeed about collaborating more intensively with different partners across all areas of our work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Earlier, I spoke about how we are involving the community through partnerships such as "GROWING TOGETHER with KidSTART" and ComLink.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members might also recall the PEERS network or the Partners Engaging and Empowering Rough Sleepers network.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Launched in July 2019, the PEERS network is a diverse group comprising Government agencies, charities, religious organisations and community groups.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked about how we assist those who have homes but are sleeping in public because of family problems.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For those who are willing to receive help, we address their immediate needs, work on underlying issues, and support them towards eventual longer term housing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There were concerns among our newfound partners that Government agencies would forcibly move the rough sleepers off the streets.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But as we continued to work with them, to look after the rough sleepers' well-being, our relationship strengthened.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Because of this trust and understanding, we were collectively able to support more rough sleepers in finding longer term solutions than if each of us were to work alone.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We welcome more partners to join us on this initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Another area that we want to partner the community more rigorously is in enhancing youth mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The latest Singapore Mental Health Study noted that young people between 18 and 34 years of age had a higher prevalence of mental health conditions, compared to older people.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mental health issues are complex but prevention, early detection and intervention can go a long way to help.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are keenly aware of the many issues and struggles faced by those with mental health issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: You have heard from my colleagues in MOE, MOH and MOM on the measures that they have taken and are taking.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The community and practitioners on the ground have also done a lot of good work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By bringing a social lens to this issue, however, we can further synergise our efforts and increase our overall impact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: A person's mental well-being affects their families neighbours, colleagues and friends.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is more than a medical issue faced by a person.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We want to address the social determinants of health – and consider what kinds of holistic support a person needs to stay healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Hence, there is more that we can do together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last month, we made an open call for persons interested in the topic of youth mental well-being to step forward, connect with us to contribute ideas, and work with us to turn some of these ideas into reality.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is yet another challenge that Deputy Prime Minister mentioned, that we are issuing to the social sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are very encouraged by the enthusiasm of all who have reached out to us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In total, as of this time, more than 700 individuals and organisations have responded and the number continues to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many are young people who are concerned by this issue and want to do something about it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Everyone who stepped forward during the open call, will have an opportunity to be part of this network.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will get to know one another, identify areas to collaborate and work together to deliver programmes and interventions, to better support our youths.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In a way, how we intend to proceed is uncharted waters.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, providing information and raising awareness about available resources so that people know where to go for help and to do so earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is just one of the points raised in the conversations we have had thus far.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I hope many Singaporeans will partner us to jointly develop solutions for a happier and healthier society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our young people deserve the best start in life possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Demand for social services will increase in both scale and complexity as our social challenges evolve.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We therefore need social service professionals with deep skills and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In April last year, we set up the Social Service SkillsFuture Tripartite Taskforce to bring together academics, professional associations, Social Service Agencies and policy-makers to look at how we can enhance the capabilities and effectiveness of the professionals in the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since then, the taskforce has initiated various manpower development projects, which we will share more on in the coming months.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides skilled and competent professionals, we also need social service agencies with the capability and capacity to deliver outcomes sustainably, effectively and efficiently.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Donors generally prefer to support programmes and services that directly benefit service users and those in need – understandably so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, resources are needed to build capability and capacity in our social service agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This fund will be made up of contributions from the Government, Tote Board and the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Thereafter, donations from FY2025 to FY2029 will be matched dollar-for-dollar.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Community Chest will also provide an additional $30 million in capital and spearhead fundraising initiatives to unlock the matching grants.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, let us grow this fund together and use it to prepare our sector for the challenges of the future.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Capability and capacity building may sound very abstract, so, let me illustrate how our efforts to build up our social service agencies capabilities can have a real and lasting impact on the people that we serve.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are many examples, but we have chosen a very "techie" one where the benefit is very clear.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Angsana Home is a Welfare Home managed by Thye Hua Kwan Moral Society in Pelangi Village.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under the Tech Booster project by the National Council of Social Service, it has implemented the SoundEye monitoring system.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The system makes use of smart sensors with AI-enabled sound recognition and motion detection technology to identify abnormal sounds or movements that could give early warning of distress from residents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Angsana Home staff can be more quickly alerted when residents require attention or help, even during night shifts when there may be fewer staff are on duty.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This allows the Home to monitor residents' safety more effectively and provide better care to residents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is an example of the kind of work that the CCT will support, enabling the social service agencies to do their work better, serve beneficiaries more effectively, have better outcomes and make the work better for social sector professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We know that building capability and capacity is a long-term effort that requires sustained investment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The CCT will give the sector the time and resources needed to build stronger and more productive social service agencies that are ready for tomorrow's challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To serve clients in a coordinated manner, we also need to strengthen the links across social service agencies, as well as between them and Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Earlier, I spoke about how we work with community agencies as equal partners so that we can operate in concert.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides working collaboratively, technology is also a key enabler to help us coordinate better.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, we harness technology to enable our clients to access services more conveniently.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides financial assistance, all SSOs offer access to employment and housing services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some also offer access to family and legal advisory services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Besides using video conferencing, we want to harness technology to provide more comprehensive and coordinated support to clients and beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, officers may ask clients to submit documents, so that they can better understand their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This may sometimes include documents that clients had already submitted to other agencies previously.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And when one agency needs to make referrals to another, officers often do so over emails for each and every case.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: After the referral is made, officers may also need to check in with their counterparts to keep track of progress.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To streamline these efforts, we will make significant system enhancements.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, the enhanced system will allow frontline officers to make faster and more comprehensive assessments about their clients' needs, through digitalisation and data sharing across multiple agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Clients will also experience greater convenience without having to repeatedly submit documents to multiple organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, the enhanced system will make it easier for agencies to refer cases, share assessments, coordinate how they are supporting their clients and monitor the clients' progress.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This way, all parties can monitor progress and coordinate follow-up actions better, to improve a client's situation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will bring agencies on-board this system progressively.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Technology is important, but it is no substitute for the human touch.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This person-to-person connection is critical in the social service sector, because it builds trust and understanding.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With mutual trust, we are comfortable calling our counterparts in another organisation and mobilising support on multiple fronts to address issues quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To strengthen these personal connections, we organise SG Cares Community Network sessions every year in each and every town, all across the island, to bring together partners from the social, health and community sectors in each town.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through this platform, partners get to affirm and build new relationships.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also invite partners to exchange ideas and best practices on addressing needs in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Community Network sessions from the first wave catalysed 60 collaborative projects. "Stories About Us", started by community partners in Hougang and Serangoon, is one such project.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These community partners saw the need to listen to the voice of those with mental health issues when designing solutions for them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They then engaged recovering mental health patients to understand the challenges they face in navigating social and healthcare services and asked them how agencies can better support them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the second wave, which we have started in November last year, our SSOs will jointly organise these sessions with community partners and volunteers, and develop and implement their ideas together with them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me now to speak briefly in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: (In Mandarin):   	Chairman, in the past few years, MSF has been collaborating with the community to strengthen our social safety net, in line with the SG Together movement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Moving forward, youth mental well-being is another important area in which we will continue with this partnership approach.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last month, I made an open call for Singaporeans interested in the topic of youth mental well-being to step forward with their ideas.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will identify areas to collaborate and work together to develop more holistic support for our youth's mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through such partnerships, we can synergise and amplify our efforts to better support Singaporeans in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I hope more Singaporeans will step forward and partner us to build a caring and inclusive society together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: (In English): Chairman, we are committed to nurturing resilient individuals, strong families and a caring society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are intervening early to give every child and every family a good start.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are continuing to put those we serve, at the centre of what we do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are partnering the community, building sector capability and strengthening networks to work better together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our society is stronger and more resilient when all Singaporeans come together, when we look out not only for ourselves, but our families, neighbours and fellow Singaporeans in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister mentioned in the Budget Statement, the Government has identified specific challenges that we are bringing partners across the public, people and private sectors together to address.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Let us work together to make Singapore a place where those in need are better supported and where Singaporeans have the chance to pursue their dreams, regardless of their starting points and what they may have encountered as they progress in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, we are building a more caring and inclusive Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: One where individuals are valued for who they are and also enabled to achieve their potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Enabling Masterplans aim to support persons with disabilities (PWDs), recognise their abilities and help them to participate meaningfully in our community and also in our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As part of the Masterplans, we set up SG Enable in 2013 to better support them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Since then, SG Enable has become a trusted partner to PWDs, their care-givers and Social Service Agencies (SSAs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Minister Desmond Lee spoke about placing citizens at the centre of our work and also the consolidation of disability support services under SG Enable in his speech earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Over the past three years, we have spoken to PWDs, care-givers, social service operators and many stakeholders, to understand the challenges and needs that they face.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: From their feedback, one common challenge is the need to work with different agencies and SSAs at different life-stages to get help, and sometimes having to submit the same documents multiple times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To them, having a single touchpoint to support them at all life-stages would make life easier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Many SSAs in the disability sector also told us that the sector could be better coordinated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, they have to work with different agencies to get approval and funding for different programmes and activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In addition, people who are willing to serve and contribute towards creating an inclusive society will be able to identify SG Enable as the single touchpoint to volunteer their time and services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Ms Denise Phua and Ms Cheryl Chan made an important point on promoting inclusion and also correcting misperceptions about PWDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This begins with building positive attitudes and improving understanding through public education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This includes reaching out to the broader community through the "See the True Me" campaign and also coming up with resources on how people should interact with PWDs, and how they can be supported at the workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Bringing different functions under one roof will improve efficiency, oversight and coordination of services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In addition, it will also provide clear direction for the many helping hands involved.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This new single-touchpoint structure is the next big step forward for the sector to bring stakeholders under one umbrella to co-create and co-deliver services and solutions for PWDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: With their input and suggestions, we are now working across the whole-of-Government, together with private and community partners, to co-create and co-deliver solutions to address the problems identified and raised during the 13 engagement sessions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Ms Denise Phua and Ms Sylvia Lim asked about what we are doing to help PWDs in terms of training and employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As announced earlier by MOM, the Government has introduced new initiatives ,such as the Enabling Employment Credit and the enhancements to the Open Door Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: That said, we are also aware that Government measures alone are not enough to meet all the needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We need to bring the public, private and people sectors together to advance inclusive employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: A good example of how we do this is through the partnership between SG Enable and SSAs to provide training and job support services and their partnership with inclusive employers, such as UOB, to run initiatives such as "The Unlimited", which helps them reach out to even more employers who are willing to employ PWDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: But of course, there is always more that we can do together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: So, under the employment workgroup, which I co-chair with Ms Denise Phua, we put ourselves in the shoes of PWDs looking for a job and we tried to understand the challenges that they face and also we have tried our best to identify the areas where they need more help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Through this exercise, we have identified four key areas where we can and we will do more to help them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Take for example, Mark, who is about to graduate from a SPED school and will be looking for a job.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: First, to enhance Mark's work capability, we will help him to improve in areas that employers have identified as crucial.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: These areas include soft skills, such as communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Second, we will create alternative supported employment models and job opportunities for Mark, as he may not be ready to work in an open employment environment yet.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Third, we will enhance employment services to match and place Mark in a job.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Fourth, we will enable Mark's colleagues to better understand and support him on the job, and we will strengthen education and awareness on working with persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: There are initiatives planned for each of these areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: One such initiative is the development of a soft skills curriculum for students with disabilities, which MOE is working with employers and SSAs on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Ms Denise Phua and other care-givers also raised concerns about a gap in terms of continual education and training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The workgroup is working with relevant people and also private sector partners to address this concern.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: All these efforts to support persons with disabilities in terms of training, work and employment are in line with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD), something that was mentioned by Ms Sylvia Lim earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Besides employment, independent living is another issue raised by persons with disabilities and their care-givers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The workgroup on independent living, which I co-chair with Ms Chia Yong Yong, is looking into how we can help persons with disabilities live more independently in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: While we recognise that there is a broad spectrum of disability types, allow me just to illustrate with the example of Amanda, who is visually impaired.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: By stepping into her shoes, we better understand the challenges that she faces along the way to access public transportation and what can enable her to overcome that.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: First, Amanda needs to cross the road from her house to the train station.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: She can activate the Green Man Plus at the pedestrian crossing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Not only does this function give her additional time to cross the road safely, the beeping sound also helps to orientate her in the right direction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: At the train station, Amanda needs to find her way to the gantry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Here, she relies on the tactile flooring to guide her to the gantry, but she needs to take out and tap her EZ-Link card.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: By using radio frequency identification or Bluetooth technology that LTA is testing, she can, in the future, pass through the gantry hands-free, without any difficulty.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: At this point, let me also extend my appreciation to Mr Cheong Kwek Bin and the Singapore Association of the Visually Handicapped (SAVH).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Working with visually impaired persons like Kwek Bin as a member of our workgroup has been immensely helpful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: He and SAVH members have provided invaluable insights on how things can be improved.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Collaborating with them has enabled us to gain insights, to use smart design and assistive technology to further help persons with disabilities to get around the built environment and also public transport.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Another example of such a collaboration was the Mobility Assistance for the Visually Impaired and Special Users (MAVIS) pilot project, earlier shared by MOT.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Many of these improvements will not only benefit persons with disabilities, but also all of us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The third Workgroup on inclusive preschools, which Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim and Assoc Prof Kenneth Poon co-chair, is studying models for inclusive preschools that will allow children with severe developmental needs to receive Early Intervention and Early Childhood services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim will elaborate more on this later.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Chairman, we are also doing more to provide support for care-givers of persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng noted that Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs) are key to supporting care-givers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: However, beyond the reduction in fees, these enhancements also provide much needed support and respite for care-givers like Mdm Valerie, who fell ill and could not take care of her daughter, Kylie.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Before joining MINDS SSCC, Kylie had to be placed in institutional care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The SSCC helped Kylie learn to be more independent in her daily living skills and also facilitated her return home to her family when her mother recovered.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Ms Rahayu Mazam asked how we could make it more convenient for persons with disabilities and their care-givers to access the support they require.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Besides making services more affordable, we are also making information more accessible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As a one-stop resource for persons with disabilities and care-givers to find help easily, it pulls together information and resources on various disability schemes and services, and guides users to make informed decisions about service options across the life stages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Sector professionals from the disability sector can also use information in the Enabling Guide to help their clients.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Ms Denise Phua and Miss Cheryl Chan also asked important questions about the support available for persons with disabilities as care-givers age, and how we can help care-givers prepare for a future where the care-givers themselves are no longer able or around to take care of their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Care-givers of persons who lack mental capacity can make financial arrangements such as setting up trust accounts with the Special Needs Trust Company.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: They can also apply to Court to be appointed as their child's deputies and have a successor deputy appointed to take their place when the need arises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Those who can live independently can tap on Government funds for Assistive Technology devices to make their lives easier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Others who require some care-giving support can consider residential options in the form of Government-funded Community Group Homes and Adult Disability Hostels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: But we also know that there are some who need greater care-giving support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: When their care-givers pass away and if no one can take over the care-giving responsibilities, the Government will step in to take care of them in Government-funded Adult Disability Homes as the last resort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In line with the suggestion by Ms Denise Phua, we will continue to work with other relevant agencies to develop the continuum of housing options for persons with disabilities, as well as to make other community services more inclusive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Chairman, I would like to speak in Mandarin now.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, we are committed to building an inclusive society where everyone can play their part, participate actively and contribute.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: SG Enable will also take the lead on public education efforts related to disability and will take over the running of the See the True Me campaign from NCSS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The changes will allow SG Enable to enhance their efficiency in coordinating resources and project planning, and reduce duplications, so that they can provide more efficient and effective services for persons with disabilities and their care-givers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In July 2019, SG Enable also launched a new online website – the Enabling Guide.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is a one-stop online platform for persons with disabilities and care-givers to find help more easily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It pulls together information and resources on various disability schemes and services, and users can make more informed decisions about different service options across life stages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Sector professionals and social service agencies can also use the information in the Enabling Guide to better help their clients.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MSF will continue to work with our people, private and public sector partners to build a more inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Under the third Enabling Masterplan, the Government has formed three cross-sectoral Workgroups to look into how we can better support persons with disabilities through their different life stages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This includes providing better support for children with developmental needs through an inclusive pre-school model, improving the employability of persons with disabilities and helping them live independently through the use of technology and design.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Workgroups will release their recommendations later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, in closing, everyone has a part to play in building a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It is about people coming together, enabling each other to create a Singapore where every individual can achieve his or her potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We want to build a Singapore that we are all proud to call home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: So, at this moment, I would like to turn over the floor to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, to speak about other MSF programmes and services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Chairman, I thank the Members for their valuable suggestions and continued support of my Ministry's work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   The Malay proverb – bend a bamboo while it is still a bamboo shoot – underlines the importance of educating children while they are still young.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Quality early childhood education helps to provide them with strong developmental foundations to succeed in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government is committed to ensure that every child has a good start in life regardless of their background.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have implemented various measures to enable more families to place their children in affordable quality pre-schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: More Malay/Muslim families are now enrolling their children in pre-schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The cohort enrolment of Malay/Muslim children aged five to six years old in pre-schools is comparable to the overall pre-school cohort enrolment for children aged five to six years old.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I hope that more Malay/Muslim parents will enrol their children in pre-schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through the various measures by the Government to improve access to affordable quality pre-schools, cost should not be a barrier for children from low-income families to receive quality early childhood education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is because they had already been means-tested for those schemes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For new enrolments from these families, we will also speed up the processing of Start-Up Grants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This grant helps to defray the initial costs of pre-school enrolment, such as uniforms and deposit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will extend more upstream support to children from low-income families, even before they enrol in pre-school, through the KidSTART programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: My Ministry works with many agencies and community partners to give every child a good start.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under Focus Area One of M3 to support marriage, parenthood and early childhood development, we partner MENDAKI on the Preschool Outreach Programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Apart from promoting awareness about the importance of pre-school, this Programme also helps Malay/Muslim families to enrol their children in pre-school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, MENDAKI and M3 partners also launched the KelasMateMatika@CC programme to help Malay/Muslim parents learn techniques to support their children aged four to six years old develop skills in Mathematics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Chairman, I have shared about the efforts by us and our community partners to provide a good start in life for all children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The responsibility of developing and educating children is a shared duty of the whole community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will become stronger if we help each other and stay united as the Malay proverb goes – like the bamboo and the river bank .

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, please come join us in creating a better future for ourselves and our future generations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Quality early childhood development helps our children build strong foundations for life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government is committed to giving every child a good start in life, regardless of their background.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the National Day Rally last year, the Prime Minister announced that the Government will continue to make quality pre-schools more affordable and accessible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since 2012, we have doubled the number of full-day pre-school places to 180,000 today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will increase to over 200,000 by 2023.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, 50% of all pre-school places are provided by Government-supported pre-schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We aim to increase this to 80% by 2025.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is the equivalent of primary school fees plus after-school student care fees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From January this year, we have raised the monthly household income ceiling for the Additional Subsidy from $7,500 to $12,000, and increased subsidies across all eligible tiers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Second, we will be extending the Partner Operator (POP) scheme for another five-year term from 2021 to 2025 and lowering the fee caps.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We aim to appoint more POP childcare centres in the new term.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They will have to meet lower monthly fee caps of $760 for full-day childcare, compared to $800 today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With this, we expect industry median fees to go down.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Fee caps for infant care will also be lowered.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Darryl David asked how the Government intends to enhance support for pre-school operators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Besides expanding the POP scheme to support more quality pre-school operators, ECDA and IMDA will launch an Industry Digital Plan for the early childhood sector later this year to provide broad-based support to help pre-schools adopt digital solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition, I am glad to announce that ECDA will extend and enhance the Support Schemes to help eligible non-Government supported pre-school operators defray various expenses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, the "Kindergarten Conversion Grant", "Enhanced Workplace Childcare Centre Scheme" and "Enhanced Social Service Agency Development Grant" help qualifying pre-school operators defray start-up costs of infrastructure development, and furniture as well as equipment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Moving forward, centres under the scheme may also qualify for support to defray their start-up infrastructure and furniture and equipment costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also increase the funding amounts for the Portable Rental Subsidy and the Teaching and Learning Resource grants which help pre-schools defray rental costs and support their quality improvements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our educators are at the heart of quality pre-schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Several efforts have been put in place over the past five years to attract more local educators and raise the quality of early childhood educators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These efforts help to raise the resilience of our early childhood workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee asked about the impact of staff on Leave of Absence due to COVID-19 on pre-schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to grow the pool of local Chinese Language Teachers, as part of our overarching strategy to make early childhood teaching a career choice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, locals can pursue the Early Childhood Chinese Language teaching track at NIEC at highly subsidised rates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Next month, NIEC will launch a new Professional Conversion Programme allowing mid-career entrants to complete the course in half the time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, from this year onward, it will be mandatory to close and teachers can have a good holiday.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This move further signals our recognition and appreciation for our pre-school educators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While we work to enhance the affordability, accessibility and quality of pre-schools for our children, we recognise that certain groups of children need additional targeted support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Desmond Choo spoke about children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We agree with him and are doing more to support this group.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC) provides young children at risk of moderate to severe developmental delays with early intervention (EI) support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The intensity of subsidised intervention is tailored to the child’s needs and is comparable to other developed countries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: EI centres also provide care-giving training to family members so that they have the skills to ensure that intervention can continue for the child beyond the centre for more sustained outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond EI centres, many pre-schools strive to adopt a more inclusive approach and enrol children with varying needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To support inclusion within pre-schools, the Government has introduced various EI programmes at pre-schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Currently, about 550 pre-schools, offer the Learning Support (LS) and Development Support (DS) programmes for children with learning and mild developmental needs respectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Pre-schools that are DS-LS providers receive Government funding to train their Learning Support Educators and procure therapy services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Early childhood educators are also taught the basics of identifying and working with children with development needs during pre-service training.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The cross-sectoral Inclusive Pre-school Workgroup, which Minister Desmond and Minister of State Sam referred to, is co-chaired by Assoc Prof Kenneth Poon and I.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are studying how to better support children with moderate and severe developmental needs in pre-schools, including the need to enhance pre-school teacher training and the role of programmes such as EIPIC and the Enhanced Pilot for Private Intervention Providers (PPIP).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are more than halfway through our work and will share our recommendations by the end of this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Besides children with developmental needs, children from low-income families is another group for whom we are providing additional targeted support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have the Pre-school Outreach Programme to reach out to low-income families to encourage them to enrol their children in pre-school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also be doing more in three ways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, we will ensure that pre-school fees is not a barrier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our recently enhanced subsidies will enable more low-income families to pay $3 per month at Anchor Operator (AOP) childcare centres, or $1 at AOP or MOE Kindergartens.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Darryl David asked about support for non-working mothers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, we enhanced support for non-working mothers under Special Approval.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under the scheme, mothers who are not working for reasons such as taking care of a younger child, studying, undergoing pregnancy, or medically unfit to work, can receive the same subsidies as working mothers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mothers who are looking for work can also qualify for Special Approval as a transitory measure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Families will not have to submit additional documents when they apply for Special Approval.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For new enrolments from these families, we will also facilitate Start-Up Grants, which defray the initial costs of enrolment such as uniforms and deposit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Allow me to illustrate how this supports families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Consider Lisa, who lives in a public rental flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Her husband is the sole breadwinner and they have a son, Caden, who recently turned two and enrolled at an AOP pre-school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Lisa is looking for a job, ECDA provided her with working mother subsidies for six months under Special Approval, and she only pays $3 per month for childcare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Previously, Lisa would have to re-apply for subsidies once her Special Approval expires in six months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With this, Lisa can have peace of mind while she seeks employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She will not have to worry about her subsidy support expiring.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, this also demonstrates the Government’s efforts to better coordinate the delivery of social services, by linking assistance schemes across pre-school, housing and social domains for families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Second, we want to ensure that children from low-income families can access developmental opportunities at their pre-schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These activities, such as field excursions, may incur some costs to families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: All AOPs are required to set aside funds to help low-income children access such opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The PSOF provides funding support for children from low-income families to participate in these developmental activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The number of children who had benefited from PSOF has increased from about 900 in 2014 to 2,400 in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the next three years, we expect this to go up to about 2,700 children per year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Third, as Minister Desmond shared, we will extend more upstream support to children from low-income families, even before they enrol in pre-school, through KidSTART.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will first expand to the Woodlands and Bedok regions this year, which have ComLink sites.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As the Government increases support for children from low-income families, we have also received active interest from many community and corporate partners wanting to do their part.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This was why my Ministry launched the "GROWING TOGETHER with KidSTART" initiative together with ComChest last September.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will enable us to deepen partnerships with interested parties to provide support in a more impactful, meaningful and sustainable manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng and Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked for an update on the partnerships that we have forged thus far.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since we launched the "GROWING TOGETHER with KidSTART" initiative last September, we have received over $800,000 in donations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This includes a sum of $600,000 which the Real Estate Developers’ Association of Singapore (REDAS) had collectively raised from its members.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Singaporeans such as Ms Joanne Lim, Founder of the Right PerspectiveSG, have also stepped forward to raise funds for KidSTART with the launch of her children’s book.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, Kimberly-Clark Corporation sponsored about 12,000 diapers for 420 KidSTART families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the next three years, they have pledged another 100,000 diapers for families on KidSTART.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Besides donations, we currently have about 250 volunteers from all walks of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They partner our officers in running activities for KidSTART families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One example is Mr Simon Loh, who is the Risk Management Director and the Chairperson of SP Heart Workers – H-E-A-R-T Workers – which is Singapore Power’s Corporate Social Responsibility Committee.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond stepping forward to volunteer when he heard about KidSTART, Simon also mobilised 30 Heart Workers to volunteer weekly at our KidSTART group sessions over four months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
