text: Besides assisting with programme delivery, they provided some very helpful suggestions to improve our activities, which we took in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We appreciate the strong commitment by all our partners and welcome more to join us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When children enter Primary school, we recognise that some parents may require after-school care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee spoke about enhancing the accessibility, affordability and quality of student care centres, or SCCs in short.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Overall, fees for registered SCCs, including those in the community, have remained stable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The current median fee is about $295 per month, close to the median of $290 per month in 2015.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For school-based SCCs, MOE puts in place measures to keep fees affordable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Operators are selected via a competitive procurement process where they are required to state any proposed fee increases throughout their six-year contract upfront.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is taken into account as part of the bidding evaluation criteria.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Contract specifications also limit the types of fees that operators can charge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Currently, SCCs registered with MSF provide sufficient capacity to meet public demand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Moving forward, we want to make sure that we regulate the sector in a manner that is conducive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: And we feel that needing to regulate the sector more tightly will have to be weighed against the increased cost and manpower requirements, on the part of both Government and SCC operators, of doing so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to monitor the student care landscape and review the requirements for SCCs as needed to ensure that they remain relevant and appropriate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Members of Parliament, we might have encountered families with children who have been abused or neglected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They need strong intervention to ensure that they have the best shot in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is why Parliament had passed amendments to the Children and Young Persons Act or CYPA last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Melvin Yong had asked for an update on the implementation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am pleased to announce that from second quarter this year, the Court will be able to grant Enhanced Care and Protection Orders, or ECPOs in short, so that all children facing abuse and neglect can benefit from enhanced protection.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With an ECPO, MSF and designated care-givers can make day-to-day and more substantive decisions for a child whose family struggles to provide a safe environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: An ECPO will minimise disruption to the child, as it can last till the child turns 21 years old.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We had earlier announced that childcare leave benefits will be extended to foster parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, I am pleased to share that from second quarter this year, these benefits will be available to 530 foster families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Foster parents will be able to use the leave when they, for example, bring foster children under their care to visit a doctor.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hear Prof Lim Sun Sun's concerns about the need to safeguard the digital rights of children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are various legislative, regulatory and public education measures in place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, new offences related to the distribution and advertising of child abuse material were introduced through the Criminal Law Reform Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Another example is the Personal Data Protection Act which all organisations must comply with when they collect, use or disclose personal data, including that of children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will not be able to completely insulate our children from online dangers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is therefore important that children learn to use the internet safely and responsibly, such as through Cyber Wellness programmes in schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Parents also play a role in keeping their children safe.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked if the Break the Silence campaign could be more inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We recognise that it is not easy for persons facing violence to seek help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Their concerns are varied, such as whether it would lead to the arrest of the perpetrator who might be a loved one, and the stigma or fear about being judged.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Violence against any person – LGBTQ or not – should not be condoned.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Penal Code and the Protection from Harassment Act protects all victims from domestic violence, regardless of their sexual orientation, gender identities or marital status.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As a policy, social services must be accessible to all, without discrimination.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, our Family Violence Specialist Centres have supported LGBTQ persons who faced violence after "coming out" to their families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In fact, I have spoken to a few of them and it is heartening to note that even when we engage the social work community, increasingly, they talk about it and see how they can look at the needs of everyone, including the LGBTQ community, friends and families in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Singapore Association for Social Workers has a Code of Professional Ethics, which is covered and reinforced throughout a social worker's training and practice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This code binds social workers to strive towards a culturally sensitive practice that acknowledges all diversity, including sexual orientation and gender identities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue our efforts to be inclusive and make social services available to all persons who require them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, MSF is exploring the setting up of a one-stop dedicated national hotline to make it even easier for victims to seek help, regardless of the type of abuse or violence they face.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A new inter-agency taskforce, which I co-chair with Senior Parliamentary Secretary Xueling, will address domestic violence regardless of family and social forms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, we continue to encourage social service agencies and social workers to deepen their capability to support all victims with empathy and sensitivity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Chairman, my colleagues and I at MSF will continue to work hard to build a society of opportunities for all Singaporeans, at every stage of their life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to transform our social safety net.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will enable Singaporeans of all abilities to participate fully in our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will give every Singaporean a good start in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We cannot do this alone and must continue to partner Singaporeans in this national journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together, we are stronger than the sum of our individual parts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: On that note, I thank Chairman and all the Members here for working with us at MSF to make life better for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Chairman, just a short clarification to Minister of State Sam Tan.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I know he has been leading Government's effort in engagement of the disability sector.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Just want to ask him what is the community's feedback to this engagement?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: And secondly, are there any specific areas that the Government is focusing on and looking to improve?

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Through these sessions, we had the opportunity to really hear for ourselves first-hand information and sharing from them.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: To many of these participants at this engagement sessions, they told us that this is the first time where they really sit down with a Ministry, Senior Management, Ministers, Mayors and all that to share their inner feelings, their frustrations, their aspirations as well as the challenges that they face.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: They also told us what they want the Government to do in order to help them.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Personally, I think this is a very useful engagement, very productive one.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Once we work out all the mechanics and schematics of all these 26 initiatives.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We plan to go back to the community to engage them again to co-create and also to co-refine all those programmes and services, so that together all these activities and initiatives are not just merely coming out from the Government, Ministries and all, but it is a joint product between the Government, the people and the private sectors.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: I think if we can do this, Singapore will truly be an inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Just building on that effort that MSF is doing that Minister of State mentioned, I wanted to just find out about the parent groups.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Because I think that is another group that you may want to also continue to build on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Because I am part of some of these organic groups and they can, I believe, augment the support structure if you empower them and also be the ambassador.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, I am just wondering with all the efforts of streamlining, having SG Enable as the one-stop point and also overseeing the See the True Me campaign, perhaps the parent groups could also be engaged and empowered to be the advocates.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I have a second clarification to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Faishal.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: He mentioned earlier that there is a sum of about $800,000 that has been donated to the KidSTART efforts through "GROWING TOGETHER with KidSTART".

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I am just wondering how would that donation be channelled through the beneficiaries as well as what are the volunteering opportunities?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If we are able to share about this more, people would be more interested and we could scale up this programme.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On that note, what is the objective of actually growing aside from just getting the support because I think there is potential to scale up KidSTART and potentially help more families.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Care-givers, the parents, form a very important key pillar in holding a family together.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So far, I was told that more than 1,600 care-givers have utilised a place to conduct sharing sessions, training and interaction sessions.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So far, 222 care-givers have registered for personal access to the Care-givers Pod.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This is only the beginning, because if we can reach out to the parents, we are able to help them chart out the plans for their children for the future.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Then, their children who either have special needs or disabilities will have a brighter future going forward.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Minister Desmond Lee and I have separately engaged, parents who are care-givers to better understand their situation, challenges and the needs that they need from the Government.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, all those engagements sessions proved to be very useful because they established trust and confidence between both sides.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We will continue to organise such engagement sessions to make sure that parents of children with disabilities or special needs will not be left alone to fend for themselves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I just want to thank the Member for the Supplementary Question and thank the Member for the interest in "GROWING TOGETHER with KidSTART".

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And that is one area that we can also empower them to be able to use that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to the opportunities available, in fact, the first basic thing is, as part of the outreach to get them on board in KidSTART.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, that is very critical, we must get them on board first.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, beyond doing all this is not only about having that donation as well as the activities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is also about developing the relationship between the donors, volunteers and the families as well as the children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to give the best start in life for every child and when we invest in such activities together, we not only give them the opportunity to have a good future, but I feel more importantly, it is also how we can get closer and we do this as part of the Singapore Together movement – where we want to do things together and build Singapore together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am very happy that the Member is very interested in this and if any individual or donors who are interested can contact ComChest or can even approach Minister Desmond Lee, Minister of State Sam Tan as well as myself at any point in time.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Let us take one last question, Dr Lily Neo.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: Minister earlier said that MSF will proactively reach out to families in HDB rental homes to assist them, to possibly buy their own HDB flats.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: Many of these families lamented that they cannot afford it.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: How does the Minister plan to do it?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: And what are the schemes in place to help them overcome this challenge?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have visited 650 families with young children door-to-door.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We aspire to reach out to 1,000 in these four locations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have a better understanding of the needs of each and every one of these families but also the assets and strengths of each family to pull themselves up, especially to make sure that poverty does not translate to the next generation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, this programme is not in and of itself targeted at achieving home ownership, though that is one of the many indicators of progress in these families' lives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When we identify that they have an aspiration for home ownership, then we will work with them to ensure that there is stability in family, stability in their work, support them with financial literacy if they wish to enhance their capabilities on that front, accumulate the savings; and then, when they are ready to pursue home ownership, there is a range of schemes available by HDB to support them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Fresh Start, for example, is one programme, but the enhanced Step-Up Grant, recently adjusted last year, will also better enable these families to leave rental housing and get back into stable housing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is a housing support team set up by HDB that will work closely with the ComLink agencies to support these families on the homeownership journey, when they make that decision.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Seah, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Chairman, on behalf of all Members who filed cuts, I would like to thank Minister Desmond Lim, Minister of State Sam Tan and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim for their considered responses, which I found very assuring.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I cannot help but notice that I have been filing cuts to MSF and the former MCYS for the last 14 Committees of Supply.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The number of cuts has been progressively coming down.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I think it shows that the Government has been resolving more issues even as new ones cropped up.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It leaves me now to thank all the men and women at MSF and all those in the social service sector for their good work, their consistent work all these years in our on-going journey to make Singapore more caring, more compassionate and a more inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: With that, Mr Chairman, I beg leave withdraw my amendment.
